target_customer: Product and marketing teams at software companies that send lifecycle messages (email, push, SMS, web) triggered by user actions
problem: Non-technical marketers and product people could not set up and test automated, event-triggered messages across channels without engineers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for messaging automation

founders.name: Dhruv Mehta
founders.background_notes: VentureBeat (2017-05-04) names him Dhruvkaran Mehta, a former Nest senior software engineer. Education not found.

founders.name: Josh Weissburg
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by VentureBeat; not listed on the YC page. A podcast summary says the founders both worked at Getaround, not opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Event ingestion and message orchestration over third party email, push and SMS providers is standard engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Message flows built in the tool created some lock in, but the product sat on commodity providers and analytics vendors could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No dated incumbent response found. Zendesk bought Outbound in May 2017 to absorb it into its Connect product.

market_need_then: VentureBeat (2017) described brands needing to message customers across SMS, email, web and push; no 2015 demand figures were found. A founder interview summary reports about $30K MRR before the exit (unopened).

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found; the name is generic and collides with outbound sales and other companies named Outbound.

outcome_analysis: Outbound was a two person YC W15 company that sold behavioral messaging and reached modest revenue by 2017 (an unverified GetLatka figure of $360K). It raised about $2.07 million in total and sold to Zendesk in May 2017 with undisclosed terms; Zendesk said Outbound would absorb its Connect product.
notes: Website outbound.io returned HTTP 503 on fetch. VentureBeat says $2.07M raised before the acquisition from Y Combinator, Subtraction Capital, Lunch Van Fund and individuals; round dates and sizes not found, so no round is recorded. Aggregators show a $1M seed (2013-11) and $400K seed (2014-09) with a $1.08M CB Insights total, unverified. PitchBook lists a deal value of $16.6M, unverified and conflicting. No dated 2015 competitor sources found.
